  Outgoing Council Member Carder congratulated Steve Johnson and Meshal
  Kash" Kashifalghita for being elected to the City Council and Mayor Hepburn
  on  being reelected. She spoke about her time on the Council and School
  District and her accomplishments on both boards. She thanked City Manager
  Russi and City staff for their support over the years. In addition, she stated

  that because the 2020 COVID pandemic, the City Council was unable
  recognize former City Council Member Charlie Rosales for his service who left
  office  in 2020.  She took a moment along with the City Council to recognize
  and thank former City Council Member Charlie Rosales who was at the
  meeting for his service to the City.

  Outgoing Council Mayor Pro Tem Davis also congratulated the newly elected
  Council  Members  and  Mayor  Hepburn  on  his reelection.  He also thanked staff
  for their support of him over the years.

  Municipal  Election  held  on  the Los Angeles County certified official canvass the following candidates were
  June  7,  2022  elected  to office.

  Steve Johnson to District 1 for a four-year term or until June of 2026

  of 2026

  other such matters as provided by law.

9.  The City Council recessed after the installation of the officers and reconvened at 7:40 p. m.

10.  Selection  of  Mayor and Mayor  Selection of Mavor and Mavor Pro Tem pursuant to Ordinance No. 1107-
  Pro Tem  Following the recess, Assistant City Clerk Estrella called for nominations, from
  the City Council for Mayor.

  Council Member Kashifalghita nominated Council Member Hepburn for Mayor.
  There were no further nominations.

  It was moved by Kash and seconded by Crosby, and unanimously carried to
  appoint Council Member Hepburn as Mayor for a one- year term until June of
  2023.

  Mayor Hepburn then called for nominations for Mayor Pro Tem.

  Council Member Lau nominated Council Member Crosby for Mayor Pro Tem.
  There were no further nominations.

  It was moved by Lau, and seconded by Kashifalghita and unanimously carried
  to appoint Rick Crosby as Mayor Pro Tem for a one- year term until June of
  2023.

14.  Fee Resolution Amendment  City Manager Russi reported on the proposed Fire Department Fees to Fee
  Resolution  No. 22- 24.  He stated that the La Verne Fire Department entered
  into an approved agreement with Fire Recovery USA for inspection services
  and incident mitigation billing, and with Dennis Grubb& Associates for Fire
  Plan Review services. As such, the Fire Department must update its 2022- 23
  fee schedule to match the fees outlined in the agreements for these services
  and  to effectively  and  accurately  recover  costs.  The updated  schedule  is
  based on actual costs of the services provided, which may include personnel,
  supplies,  and  equipment.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was none.

  It was moved by Johnson, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried to adopt
  Resolution No. 22- 54 amending the fee Resolution No. 22- 24 with the updated
  Fire Department fees.
